facts.fact: Tom Doak (Renaissance Golf Design), opened 2001, on the bluff above the Pacific north of Bandon Dunes.
The grey whale's tail was the course chat's suggestion, approved 2026-10-21.

current.subject: A grey whale's tail rising from a block of sea.
current.keep: The fluke: a strong, symmetric silhouette and the ocean in one shape.
current.weaknesses: The rectangle of water is as big as the tail and the drips clutter it; the fluke's shape is soft.

concepts.name: The Fluke
concepts.rationale: The tail is the whole mark now: a crisp, symmetric fluke with a notched trailing edge, barnacle patches and a single ring of foam where it leaves the water.
references: Grey whales off the Oregon coast
concepts.symbolism: The moment before the dive: the Pacific showing itself, as the course does.
concepts.typography: Cormorant Garamond SemiBold capitals: an ocean-liner elegance that matches the symmetry.
concepts.strengths: Clean silhouette, reads at any size, embroiders well.
concepts.tradeoffs: Whale tails are a common coastal motif; this one is better, not more ownable.

concepts.name: The Sand Wave
concepts.rationale: A dune drawn as a breaking wave, crested with fescue, the Pacific curling in beneath. Pacific Dunes is a course of dunes beside an ocean; the mark makes them one shape.
concepts.symbolism: Sand that moves like water: the dunes are the waves of this course.
concepts.interpretation: The dune-as-wave is a visual metaphor, not a real landform on the course.
concepts.typography: Fraunces SemiBold, soft-cornered and modern, picks up the curl.
concepts.strengths: A single, original idea no other club owns; striking silhouette.
concepts.tradeoffs: Some will see a wave before they see sand.

recommendation: Concept 2. The Sand Wave is the most original idea in the Bandon set and says 'dunes by the Pacific' in one shape. The fluke stays a fine alternative.
